subject.title: Feature: Per-spawn tool restrictions for sub-agents

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `tools: "none" | { allow?: string[]; deny?: string[] }` as the durable per-spawn `sessions_spawn` security contract, including deny-wins semantics and fail-closed handling for runtimes that cannot enforce the policy?
rationale: This chooses a new public agent-tool API and a lasting security boundary; source evidence supports the need, but cannot determine the intended compatibility and runtime-policy contract without maintainer direction.

options.title: Approve the durable deny-wins contract
options.body: Adopt the linked PR’s object-or-`none` policy shape, persist it immutably on child sessions, and require complete cross-runtime enforcement proof.

options.title: Ship an allow-only first version
options.body: Reduce the initial surface to explicit allowlists and `none`, deferring deny-based policies until all runtimes can enforce them consistently.

options.title: Keep global and per-agent policy only
options.body: Decline dynamic per-spawn restrictions and retain existing coarser configuration, leaving the reported isolation workflows unsupported.

recommendation.title: Approve the durable deny-wins contract
recommendation.body: Adopt the linked PR’s object-or-`none` policy shape, persist it immutably on child sessions, and require complete cross-runtime enforcement proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion identifies this person as the maintainer-facing reviewer for the API shape, and the active contributor requested their contract confirmation.
